content.title: Is there a launch today? NASA, SpaceX, Blue Origin launch schedule in Florida
content.text: April 1, 2026Updated April 15, 2026, 3:08 p.m. ETFlorida's Space Coast hosted a record-shattering 109 orbital rocket launches during 2025, soaring beyond all previous annual records.Will this year's final total surpass that lofty sum from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and NASA's Kennedy Space Center? By the end of March, 22 rockets had taken flight from the Sunshine State.Looking ahead, the Cape's April launch schedule will feature the usual heavy diet of SpaceX Starlink satellite missions — with space fans anticipating Blue Origin's next New Glenn rocket launch.Following are the latest missions coming up from the Cape. All launches are listed in Eastern Daylight Time. But be aware: Dates and times routinely change for a wide variety of reasons.FLORIDA TODAY's Space Team provides live blog coverage of each launch at floridatoday.com/space, starting at least 90 minutes before liftoff. For questions or comments, email Space Reporter Rick Neale at Rneale@floridatoday.com. No earlier than Sunday, April 19: Blue Origin New Glenn-3Mission:A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket will launch AST SpaceMobile’s next-generation Block 2 BlueBird satellite to low-Earth orbit, marking Blue Origin's third launch from Cape Canaveral, a Federal Aviation Administration operations plan advisory shows.Launch window: 6:45 a.m. to 12:19 p.m.Trajectory: TBA.Location: Launch Complex 36 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station.Sonic booms: No.Live FLORIDA TODAY Space Team coverage: Starts two hours before liftoff at floridatoday.com/space.Monday, April 20: SpaceX GPS III-8Mission: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket will launch a GPS III space vehicle for the Space Force on a national security mission, a Federal Aviation Administration operations plan advisory shows.Launch window: 2:48 a.m. to 4:05 a.m.Trajectory: TBA.Location: Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station.Sonic booms: TBALive FLORIDA TODAY Space Team coverage: Starts 90 minutes before liftoff at floridatoday.com/space.First half of 2026: Blue Origin Blue Moon PathfinderMission: A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket will launch a Blue Moon lunar lander carrying NASA payloads on a demonstration
